newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares end lower in sluggish weekend trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares end lower in sluggish weekend trade.

text.p: ** (1230 GMT) Indian shares drift lower, undercurrent seen
weak next week
** Cautious participants stay on sidelines in anticipation of
crucial political developments
** Heavy activity in bank stocks, sellers abound ahead of
many new floats
** Benchmark Bombay index sheds 2.99 pts, the National
exchange index loses 0.73 pts and the Delhi index
falls 4.04 pts
Indian shares closed broadly lower in range-bound light trade on Friday as cautious participants kept to the sidelines ahead of the weekend, brokers said.
"It was a dull day," said one dealer at a foreign broking firm. "People are watching political developments."
He said players kept away in anticipation of a long-awaited police report on a bribery scandal involving former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao.
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index closed 2.99 points, or 0.09 percent, lower at 3,346.78.
The ruling minority coalition government of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda is dependent on Rao's Congress party for its survival.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index eased 0.73 points to 977.03. The net traded value was 9.43 billion rupees in 45.45 million shares.
The 500-share CRISIL index shed 2.42 points, or 0.37 percent, to 656.51.
Traders said bank shares attracted heavy activity ahead of SBI's $400 million Euroissue and domestic floats by several state-run banks.
SBI closed up 0.10 rupees at 263.55 in volume of 22.16 million shares on the NSE. The share gained 0.25 to 263.25 on the BSE with over 5.5 million shares traded.
Oriental Bank shed 0.55 rupees to 69.30 and Bank of Rajasthan 0.65 to 143.60 on the NSE.
The BSE National index fell 14.65 points to 1,494.45, the Delhi index 4.04 points to 742.65 and the Madras index 5.41 points to 3,437.79.
The Calcutta index nudged 0.42 points higher at 432.07 but the undercurrent was subdued, traders said.
--RANJIT GANGADHARAN, Bombay Newsroom +91-22-265-9000
